::: {#thm-transitive-composition}
#### Transitive relations contain their squares

Let $R$ be a relation on a set $S$ (@rem-relation-on-set).
Then $R$ is transitive (@def-transitive) if and only if $R^2 \subseteq R$ (@def-relation-power).

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

($\Rightarrow$)
Suppose $R$ is transitive, and let $(a, c) \in R^2 = R \circ R$.
By the definition of composition (@def-relation-composition),
$a \mathrel{R} b$ and $b \mathrel{R} c$ for some $b \in S$.
Since $R$ is transitive, $a \mathrel{R} c$.
So $R^2 \subseteq R$ (@def-subset).

($\Leftarrow$)
Suppose $R^2 \subseteq R$,
and let $a \mathrel{R} b$ and $b \mathrel{R} c$.
Then $(a, c) \in R \circ R = R^2$, by the definition of composition,
so $(a, c) \in R$.
So $R$ is transitive.

:::

:::
